July increase: 1.3

python3 << 'EOF'
# Data from October 1939 bulletin (page 62) - cumulative seigniorage on silver and minor coins
# Table shows values in millions of dollars

cumulative = {
    'June': 73.4,
    'July': 74.7,
    'August': 76.1,
    'September': 80.1
}

# Calculate monthly increases
july_increase = cumulative['July'] - cumulative['June']
august_increase = cumulative['August'] - cumulative['July']
september_increase = cumulative['September'] - cumulative['August']

print(f"July increase: {july_increase}")
print(f"August increase: {august_increase}")
print(f"September increase: {september_increase}")

# Calculate z-score relative to July and August
import statistics

baseline = [july_increase, august_increase]
mean_baseline = statistics.mean(baseline)
stdev_baseline = statistics.stdev(baseline)  # sample stdev with n-1

print(f"\nMean of July & August: {mean_baseline}")
print(f"Sample stdev: {stdev_baseline}")

z_score = (september_increase - mean_baseline) / stdev_baseline
print(f"\nZ-score: {z_score}")
print(f"Z-score rounded to nearest hundredths: {round(z_score, 2)}")

# Determine if statistically unusual (z > 1.96 for 5% significance)
is_unusual = z_score > 1.96
print(f"\nSeptember statistically unusual (|z| > 1.96)? {is_unusual}")
print(f"Answer: [{round(z_score, 2)}, {'unusual' if is_unusual else 'normal'}]")
EOF
